name: project_path_doctor
purpose: Windows PATH auditor that reports dead entries, duplicates and shadowed executables, resolving machine and user PATH in true composition order.
notes: First Rust project on this machine, chosen as a workflow shakedown. Read-only by design: it reports, it never writes PATH. Born from real PATH shadowing hit during machine provisioning on 2026-09-15. Slice 1 is complete - registry reading and composition (winreg, chosen over the windows crate so the unsafe stays in the dependency), per-entry findings, executable enumeration with PATHEXT read from the environment, shadow resolution for both the running process and a fresh one, and the output layer with a versioned JSON contract in docs/SPEC.md. A GUI is a confirmed consumer, so the serialisation shape is defined once in pathdoc-core behind a serde feature rather than mirrored in the front end; it is at schemaVersion 4. Schema 2 replaced a conflicts-only shadows array with a full executables array after three of the four names worth reporting turned out to appear exactly once; schema 3 added live process positions after the tool was found to name the wrong winner for any name present in both a runtime-injected directory and a registry one. Exit 1 is reserved for actionable per-entry findings; shadowing is reported always and gates only under --fail-on-shadow. The acceptance test doubles as a drift canary for the machine's PATH and has caught two unannounced changes; volatile counts are isolated at the top of it. Shell-level masking detection landed at schemaVersion 4: PowerShell aliases and functions that answer to a name before PATH is searched, 24 of them here including sc hiding sc.exe. It extends the per-name executables records rather than being a Finding or a separate section. intercepts is a list and the report names every interpreter consulted, because the verdict is per shell - curl is masked in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and clear in PowerShell 7, verified with --shell powershell --shell pwsh - and because listed-as-consulted is what turns an absent record into asked-and-clear rather than never-asked. Defaults to -NoProfile so the tool never executes user code unasked, and never gates the exit code. Registry access has been extracted into a winenv crate that knows nothing about PATH, so the planned env-var tool depends on it rather than on pathdoc-core: dependencies point from each tool at winenv, never from one tool at another. Decided: winenv stays in this repository, unpublished, and this repository becomes the toolkit workspace with the tools as members when the env-var tool exists - which bends the trunk's one-repo-per-project convention deliberately, for the trunk to amend when the restructure happens. Dual licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 with both licence files present, ready to publish. Tooling entry point is the justfile - just check runs fmt, clippy in both feature configurations, nextest and cargo-deny. GitHub Actions runs the full gate on windows-latest and only fmt-check plus deny on ubuntu-latest, because the workspace cannot build for Linux at all. CI earned its place on its third run by going red on the masking scan: a runner exceeded the ten-second timeout that measures 150 ms here, which exposed three real defects - a timed-out child abandoned rather than killed (nextest reported it as LEAK on a test that passed, and it would have leaked one shell per audit in a long-lived consumer such as the GUI), three portable tests that assumed a live interpreter would answer, and interpreter deduplication running against the ones that had already answered rather than before spawning. Fixed by making the script cheap - Get-Alias plus the Function: drive rather than Get-Command -CommandType Alias,Function, 197 constructs against 1391 with identical results - with the timeout raised to 30 seconds as a hedge rather than a fix. The local 149ms-vs-218ms delta understated it: autoload discovery scales with the number of installed modules, so what was removed is a cost that grows with the host rather than a 69ms constant, which is why a runner blew a limit this machine never approached. Green on run 4: zero LEAK markers, no test over ten seconds. Portable tests no longer ask an external process what the machine is configured like - the shell scan runs against an injected fake - though cmd.exe and icacls are still spawned where the process behaviour is itself under test and the assertion is a marker file or an ACL rather than a duration. The one real-interpreter test lives in this_machine.rs and skips loudly. 174 tests. Published and installable: cargo install --git https://github.com/chamal-code/pathdoc pathdoc-cli --locked works despite publish = false, which only blocks crates.io. Version stays 0.1.0 deliberately - the JSON contract is at schemaVersion 4 and roadmap items that would change it are outstanding, so 0.x is the accurate claim and 1.0.0 would promise stability nobody decided to offer. A second workflow, release.yml, triggers on v* tags: a gate job runs check-portable and verifies the tag matches Cargo.toml, then a release job holding the only contents: write in the repository builds --locked and publishes. The privileged job deliberately runs no third-party action - first-party checkout, the preinstalled toolchain, and the preinstalled gh CLI - so the writable token is never in a job executing somebody else's code, and event values reach PowerShell through env: rather than being interpolated into a script body. Requires the repository default_workflow_permissions to be read and write; it is capped at read until raised, which 403s. The artifact is a zip carrying pathdoc.exe plus LICENSE-APACHE, LICENSE-MIT and README.md, because Apache-2.0 section 4 requires the licence to travel with a redistribution, plus a separate SHA256SUMS.txt. The binary is unsigned and the README says so plainly with the checksum command, since SmartScreen will warn and nothing but a code-signing certificate can change that. Release notes live in .github/release-notes-template.md rather than a here-string in the workflow: a PowerShell here-string terminator must start its line while a YAML block scalar requires indentation, so the two cannot coexist - found by parsing the YAML rather than by a failed release. README now opens with concrete symptoms in the words somebody would search (git vendored inside another application, node/npx resolving to the wrong version, diff and sc being aliases, a dead PATH entry, python as a Store stub, a build broken by a PATH change), then what it will not do (never writes, never uses the network, runs no profile code unless asked), then Install, then a For automated use section carrying the three facts an agent needs: --json with schemaVersion, exit codes 0/1/2, and read capabilities before trusting an empty list. 0.1.1 is a hotfix cut before any winget submission: four em dashes in the clap doc comments in options.rs reached --help and printed as mojibake on a non-UTF-8 console, the same defect class already fixed in the report renderer. The ASCII test covered the report and not clap, so it passed the whole time - the durable fix is the new no_non_ascii_reaches_a_terminal test in options.rs, which covers long help, short help, --version and four error paths, and was proved to fail by reintroducing the character. Held before submission rather than left to the next release because a winget manifest pins an artifact URL and hash, so shipping it would have cost a 0.1.1 release plus a second PR to a Microsoft repo to undo. v0.1.1 is released and is the version prepared for winget: manifests complete and winget validate passing, InstallerSha256 FE7F...A4C7 fetched from the published SHA256SUMS.txt and confirmed against the downloaded artifact, ReleaseDate 2026-09-16 from published_at in UTC - the local-time conversion gives 2026-09-17 here, and that trap fired for real. All seven URLs answer 200 including the README licence anchor checked by fetching the tagged raw file, RelativeFilePath confirmed against the published zip's entries, and the published binary re-verified clean on all eight output paths. While the release did not yet exist the two unknowable fields were held as placeholders that deliberately failed winget validate, which is the pattern to repeat: a stale-but-plausible value would validate cleanly while pointing at the wrong artifact. Known gap deferred to 0.2.0 and recorded in the SPEC roadmap: the binary carries no Windows VERSIONINFO resource, verified empty, so Explorer properties and PowerShell inventory cannot identify it; fixing it needs a build-dependency and therefore a cargo deny allow-list change, which does not belong in a hotfix. v0.1.0 was released: annotated tag on 36f442c, both release jobs green first run, two assets published, and the artifact verified from the public URL by a third party - zip 443575 bytes, sha256 a46b703a...efc46b matching SHA256SUMS.txt, LICENSE-APACHE in the archive byte-identical to apache.org's canonical text. The repo default_workflow_permissions had to be raised from read to write for the release job; the per-job scoping is what made that safe. winget manifests are authored by hand under .winget/manifests/c/chamal-code/pathdoc/0.1.0/ at schema 1.12.0, mirroring the winget-pkgs path so a submission is a copy rather than a reconstruction: identifier chamal-code.pathdoc, InstallerType zip with NestedInstallerType portable because the exe sits inside a version-named top-level directory, Moniker pathdoc so winget install pathdoc works without the full identifier, and 15 symptom-word tags. winget validate passes and all seven URLs answer 200. The InstallerSha256 is copied from the published SHA256SUMS.txt and was verified against the downloaded artifact rather than recomputed, and RelativeFilePath was checked against the published zip's actual entries. .winget/README.md carries the per-release checklist, which is eight version-bearing lines plus the directory name and ReleaseDate - notably the tagged LicenseUrl, ReleaseNotesUrl and Documentations URLs, which fail silently because they still resolve. Deliberately not automated and not referenced from any workflow. The PR to microsoft/winget-pkgs is the owner's action, not this session's. Next is the roadmap: decoding WindowsApps stubs, the env-var backup/diff tool, and an automated shadowing cross-check against Get-Command.
